questions.question: The volume of a tank is 72 cubic meters. Water is poured into it at the rate of 60 liters per minute. How much time till it takes to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given :**

Volume of the tank = 72 m³

Water is poured at a rate of 60 litres/minute 

**Formula used :**

1 m³ = 1000 litres 

**Calculations :**

Total volume of Water (in litres) = 72 × 1000 = 72000 litres 

Total time taken = Total volume/Rate of water poured per minute 

⇒ Total time = 72000/60

⇒ 1200 minutes 

⇒ 20 hours (1 hour = 60 minutes) 

**∴ The total time taken was 20 hours **

questions.question: Ratnesh and Vineet worked on alternate days, starting with Ratnesh. The entire work got completed in 54(3)/(4) days. If Ratnesh alone can finish the work in 48 days, then in how many days can Vineet alone do the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratnesh and Vineet worked on alternate days, starting with Ratnesh.

The entire work got completed in 54(3)/(4) days.

If Ratnesh alone can finish the work in 48 days

**Concept Used:**

Using LCM method

**Calculation:**

Ratnesh alone can finish the work in 48 days

Ratnesh’s one day work = 1/48

Ratnesh and Vineet complete the whole work in = 54(3)/(4) days

Ratnesh and Vineet work on alternate days, with Ratnesh beginning so, we can say Ratnesh will work only 27(3/4) days Vineet will work only 54(3/4) - 27(3/4) = 27 days

If Ratnesh’s one day work = 1/48 of work A complete in = 1 days

Ratnesh’s 27(3/4) days work = (1/48)(27(3/4) = 111/192

Remaining work = 1 - 111/192 = 81/192

Vineet complete 81/192 work in = 27 days

⇒ Vineet complete whole work in = 192 × 27/81 = 64 days

**∴ Vineet alone can do the work in 64 days.**

questions.question: 55 workers can finish a work in 16 days. For finishing the same work in 10 days, how many more workers are required?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

55 workers can finish a work in 16 days.

Time required to finish the same work = 10 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Number of Workers × Number of Days

**Calculation:**

Let the number of additional workers required be x.

Total work = 55 × 16

⇒ Total work = 880

New number of workers required to finish the work in 10 days = 880 / 10

⇒ New number of workers required = 88

Additional workers required = 88 - 55

⇒ Additional workers required = 33

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: 25 men can complete a task in 16 days. Four days after they started working, 5 more men, with equal workmanship, joined them. How many days will be needed by all to complete the remaining task?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

25 men do the task in 16 days

5 more men had joined them 

**Formula Used:**

If M₁ men can finish W₁ work in D₁ days and M₂ men can finish W₂ work in D₂ days then,

(M₁ × D₁)/W₁ = (M₂ × D₂)/W₂

**Calculation:**

Total work done by 25 men = 25 × 16 = 400 units

Work done in 1st four days = 25 × 4 = 100 units

Remaining work = 400 - 100 = 300 units

Numbers of men joined = 5

Total number of men = 25 + 5 = 30

Remaining work done by 30 men in x days

300 = 30 × x

x = 10

**∴ 10 days will be needed by all to complete the remaining task**

questions.question: 8 men or 10 boys can complete a work in 174 days. 12 men and 14 boys will complete the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

8 men or 10 boys can complete a work in 174 days.

**Formula:**

Work = (Men × Days)/(Rate)

**Solution:**

Let the rate of one man be m and the rate of one boy be b.

8m = 10b

m/b = 5/4

Efficiency of Men = 5 and Boys = 4

(12m + 14b) × Days = (8m × 174 days)

(12 × 5 + 14 × 4) × Days = (8 × 5 × 174 days)

(12 × 5 + 14 × 4) × Days = (8 × 5 × 174 days)

116 × Days = (8 × 5 × 174)

6960/116 = 60 Days 

Days = 60

**Therefore, 12 men and 14 boys will complete the same work in 60 days.**

questions.question: 15 people working 6 hours per day earn Rs. 900. How much money will 20 people earn, working 10 hours per day?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of persons working (M₁) = 15

Working hours/day (T₁) = 6 hours

Wages earned by 15 persons (W₁) = Rs. 900/day

Number of persons (M₂) = 20

Working hours/day (T₂) = 10 hours

**Formula used:**

(M₁ × D₁ × T₁)/W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × T₂)/W₂

**Calculation:**

According to the question

(M1 × D1 × T1)/W1 = (M2 × D2 × T2)/W2

⇒ (15 × 1 × 6)/900 = (20 × 1 × 10)/W₂

⇒ 90/900 = 200/W₂

⇒ 1/10 = 200/W₂

⇒ W₂ = (10 × 200)

⇒ W₂ = Rs. 2000

**∴ The required money earned by 20 persons working 10 hours per day is Rs. 2000**

questions.question: A contractor employed 69 workers to complete a work in 20 days. How many more workers he should employ to complete the work in 12 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the constant work rule: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

69 × 20 = M₂ × 12

Total workers required (M₂) = 1380 ÷ 12 = 115

Additional workers needed = 115 − 69 = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46 workers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of workers (M₁) = 69

Initial number of days (D₁) = 20

Target number of days (D₂) = 12

**Formula Used:**

Since the total work remains constant, we use the formula: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work in man-days = 69 × 20

⇒ Total work = 1380 units

⇒ Let M₂ be the total number of workers required to complete the work in 12 days.

⇒ M₂ × 12 = 1380

⇒ M₂ = 1380 ÷ 12

⇒ M₂ = 115 workers

⇒ The contractor already has 69 workers.

⇒ Number of more workers needed = Total required workers − Initial workers

⇒ Number of more workers = 115 − 69

⇒ Number of more workers = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46 workers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule (Chain Rule)

The generalized formula for man-days calculations is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M = Men, D = Days, H = Hours, and W = Work.

Time and Efficiency Relationship

Time taken to complete a specific task is inversely proportional to the efficiency or the number of workers. More workers mean fewer days required.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in direct proportion to the amount of total work completed by the individual, or in the ratio of their efficiencies if everyone works for an equal number of days.

questions.question: A certain number of persons can complete a work in 90 days. If there be 10 persons less, it would have taken 10 days more for the work to be completed. Find the total number of persons in the beginning.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by certain number of persons = 90 days

Difference in days if 10 persons less = 10 days

**Concept:**

Work is inversely proportional to time

**Solution:**

⇒ Let original number of persons be x

⇒ Work done is same, so x*90 = (x-10)*100

⇒ 90x = 100x - 1000

⇒ x = 100

**Therefore, the total number of persons in the beginning was 100.**

questions.question: To finish a work, P takes half of the number of days required by Q to finish it. If they together can finish the work in 36 days, then in how many days Q alone can finish the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P takes half of the number of days required by Q to finish the work.

P and Q together can finish the work in 36 days.

**Formula used:**

Work done together = 1/P + 1/Q

**Calculation:**

Let Q alone can finish the work in Q days.

⇒ P alone can finish the work in Q/2 days.

⇒ 1/(Q/2) + 1/Q = 1/36

⇒ 2/Q + 1/Q = 1/36

⇒ 3/Q = 1/36

⇒ Q = 36×3

⇒ Q = 108 days

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: A, B and C can complete a work in 12, 15 and 20 days, respectively. How many days are required to finish the work if they work together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 12 days

Time taken by B to complete the work = 15 days

Time taken by C to complete the work = 20 days

**Formula used:**

Time required to complete the work when A, B, and C work together = 1 / (Total work done by A, B, and C together in 1 day)

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1 / 12

Work done by B in 1 day = 1 / 15

Work done by C in 1 day = 1 / 20

Total work done by A, B, and C together in 1 day = 1 / 12 + 1 / 15 + 1 / 20

Finding a common denominator:

LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60

Work done by A, B, and C together in 1 day = (5 + 4 + 3) / 60 = 12 / 60 = 1 / 5

Time required to complete the work = 1 / (1 / 5) = 5 days

**∴ The work will be completed in 5 days if A, B, and C work together.**
